In this step, you select which data you want to collect from your Kubernetes cluster.

While there are many different types of data you can collect, this journey focuses on a few to get you started. Activating more toggles can increase metrics consumption and cost.

To select data to collect, complete the following steps:

1. In **Cluster name**, enter the name of your cluster.

   If you don't know the cluster name, run:

   ```
   kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[].name}{"\n"}'
   ```

1. In **Namespace**, replace `default` with the namespace where you want to deploy monitoring infrastructure.

1. In **Platform**, select your platform:

   - Kubernetes, including EKS on EC2 and GKE.
   - Amazon EKS on AWS Fargate. [Node Exporter](/docs/grafana-cloud/monitor-infrastructure/kubernetes-monitoring/configuration/manage-configuration/#node-exporter) metrics are disabled.
   - Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).
   - Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot.
   - IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service.
   - Red Hat OpenShift.

1. In **Kubernetes Cluster monitoring**, enable **Cluster metrics** and **Cluster Events**.

> **Caution:** No other toggles are required for this learning path. Enabling additional toggles can increase metrics consumption.

The following image shows what your feature monitoring selections should look like.
